summary: Intro discovery focused on security posture for potential Redwood deployment (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Customer cares about SOC2/ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and retention. Agreed to send docs and schedule technical deep-dive.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we’ll do a quick intro and then dive into your security questions. I’m Jordan, AE at Redwood, and I have Priya from our security/infra team.
[00:07] Marcus Grant: Hey Jordan, thanks. Marcus here, CTO at Cobalt Tech. Leah from security is on as well.
[00:12] Leah Kim: Hi all.
[00:14] Priya Nair: Hi, thanks. Quick question on scope - are you looking at hosted Redwood API or a Dedicated/Private deployment?
[00:22] Marcus Grant: We’re evaluating all three. For POC we might try Hosted but at enterprise scale we want Dedicated or Private in our VPC. Main blockers are SOC2/ISO certs, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration.
[00:36] Jordan Lee: Understood. Priya, do you want to walk through our standard posture?
[00:39] Priya Nair: Sure. Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II, and we have ISO 27001 in progress for a couple of regions, uh, depends on timeline. For Hosted customers we provide tenant isolation, encryption at rest using customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private, and optional HSM integrations for high-assurance keys.
[00:58] Leah Kim: When you say customer-managed KMS, do you support cross-account keys in AWS, or is it a Redwood-managed key?
[01:06] Priya Nair: Good question. For Hosted default is Redwood-managed keys for convenience, but for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys in their AWS account (cross-account IAM roles) and bring-your-own-key flows. On-prem we can integrate with enterprise HSMs as well.
[01:22] Daniel Park: Are there egress concerns? We need proof that payloads don’t leave region X and, um, that logs with sensitive PII are scrubbed or routed to our secured logging.
[01:32] Jordan Lee: Yes, we have region-aware routing and data residency controls. For Dedicated and Private you can restrict all egress to your VPC and route audit logs to your S3 or Splunk via secure delivery. We’ll share a network diagram.
[01:44] Marcus Grant: Audit logs: what detail do you capture? We need full request/response-level auditing for compliance, but also worry about storing sensitive output.
[01:53] Priya Nair: We capture request metadata, timestamps, user IDs, model/route, and operational logs. Full response content capture is optional — default for Hosted does not persist full responses unless configured for logging; Dedicated/Private gives you full control and you can ship logs to your own retention store. We also support field-level redaction and token-level filtering if needed.
[02:14] Leah Kim: Are those logs tamper-evident? Do you support append-only storage or signed logs?
[02:19] Priya Nair: We support write-once S3 buckets and can provide log signing with KMS. For higher assurance we can work with your compliance team to enable audit log immutability using your storage.
[02:31] Marcus Grant: Encryption in transit?
[02:33] Jordan Lee: TLS 1.2+ and mutual TLS is available for Dedicated/private endpoints.
[02:38] Daniel Park: For SSO: we use Okta and have SAML IdP. How do you support SAML and SCIM?
[02:45] Priya Nair: We support SSO via SAML 2.0 and OIDC, and we support SCIM provisioning for user sync. RBAC is role-based with least-privileges; you can map IdP groups to Redwood roles. We have an enterprise SSO guide - we’ll share it.
[03:03] Leah Kim: For RBAC, can we get fine-grained roles for model access and environment separation?
[03:08] Priya Nair: Yes, you can define per-route and per-model permissions; e.g., dev team vs production team. We also support token scoping and short-lived creds for automation.
[03:18] Marcus Grant: SOC2 is a must. Can you send your report and also describe change control and vulnerability management?
[03:25] Jordan Lee: Absolutely. We’ll send SOC 2 Type II and our security whitepaper. Priya, quick on vuln mgmt?
[03:31] Priya Nair: We run regular internal and external pen-tests, quarterly vuln scans, and have a documented change control process with approvals and rollback. We also do dependency scanning and container hardening.
[03:41] Daniel Park: How about model artifacts and KV cache—are cached embeddings considered customer data?
[03:47] Priya Nair: Cache is configurable; for Hosted we might cache prefixes to improve latency, but for Dedicated/Private you can disable caching or keep it ephemeral in memory only. When using persistent caches we support encryption and tenancy boundaries.
[03:59] Marcus Grant: Data retention policy—we keep data for 90 days; can you align or let us set retention?
[04:05] Jordan Lee: Yes, retention is configurable. For Hosted you can opt out of retention; for Dedicated/Private you control retention via your logs S3 lifecycle. We’ll document the retention controls.
[04:16] Leah Kim: Legal — do you support data processing agreements and specific liability clauses?
[04:21] Jordan Lee: We have standard DPA language and can discuss enterprise amendments during procurement. Our legal team is used to working with enterprise security teams.
[04:30] Marcus Grant: For POC we’d like to test latency and run a few evals. If we go to Dedicated, what's the onboarding time?
[04:37] Priya Nair: Dedicated onboarding is typically 4-6 weeks depending on infra work and whether you need private networking. Private/VPC deployments can be longer if on-prem options and HSM integrations are required.
[04:47] Marcus Grant: Understood. Can we get a list of supported compliance certs per region?
[04:52] Jordan Lee: Yes, we have a region-by-region compliance matrix, we’ll attach it.
[04:56] Aisha Rahman: One quick thing — uptime SLAs?
[04:59] Jordan Lee: Hosted has best-effort but we’ll provide usage guidance; Dedicated comes with SLA options and error budgets, and Private is negotiated.
[05:09] Daniel Park: For keys — can the KMS live in our account and you assume minimal privileges? We need key rotation policies to be enforced on our side.
[05:17] Priya Nair: Yes, customer-managed KMS in your account is supported and key rotation policies remain yours. We use cross-account roles with least privilege to encrypt/decrypt ephemeral blobs.
[05:28] Marcus Grant: Any known gaps? E.g., are there any compliance items you don’t support today?
[05:33] Priya Nair: Right now, ISO 27701 / some regional certifications might be in-progress depending on region. We’re transparent about roadmaps and can provide timelines.
[05:42] Jordan Lee: Okay let’s recap next steps and owners. We’ll send SOC2, network diagram, SSO guide, and a Dedicated pilot pricing sheet. Priya will prep the VPC and KMS checklist. Marcus will share retention policy and compliance contact.
[05:56] Leah Kim: Sounds good. Also, please indicate any egress controls and how logs are scrubbed prior to storage.
[06:03] Priya Nair: Noted, we’ll include log redaction options in the doc set.
[06:08] Jordan Lee: Great — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the deep-dive. Thanks everyone.
[06:12] Marcus Grant: Thanks Jordan, Priya.
[06:14] Leah Kim: Thanks.
[06:15] [END OF TRANSCRIPT]
notes: Attendees requested SOC2 report, SSO/SAML integration guide, VPC/network diagram, and Dedicated pilot pricing. Customer leaning toward Dedicated/Private for production due to data residency and KMS requirements.
